messages:
tom_h: FYI alert from backup-monitor: abnormal object size variance for tenant-52 archives in us-east-1. some snapshots are tiny (few KB) but expected ~GB. looks like metadata stripped.

nina.ops: did uploader change? we rolled backup-uploader v2.4.0 last night.

tom_h: logs show 204 responses from our archive PUTs but S3 response headers missing `x-amz-server-side-encryption`.

ops_lead: that implies uploads landed without SSE-S3 or CMEK. risky. any pattern (tenants, regions)?

infra_sam: quick grep: all affected objects have header `User-Agent: backup-uploader/2.4.0` and principal arn:aws:iam::111:role/backup-uploader-prod. older objects (pre-rollout) have SSE headers.

sec_bot: rule sse-enforcement triggered: put-object without server-side-encryption. count=18 tenants affected, regions=[us-east-1, eu-west-1].

nina.ops: rollback backup-uploader to 2.3.7 now?

ops_lead: hold on. we need to confirm cause. devs: what changed in 2.4.0?

infra_sam: changelog says "refactor HTTP client; rely on SDK's default header behavior". suspect SDK change removed explicit SSE header we were injecting.

tom_h: also saw one codepath that falls back to simple PUT when multipart init fails; that path doesn't attach encryption headers. multipart init failures correlate with an IAM policy change we pushed last week that narrowed sts:AssumeRole for the uploader role.

sec_bot: correlation: iam-policy-change event 2026-04-03T02:01:12Z touched role/backup-uploader-prod. cloudtrail shows AssumeRoleDenied for multipart-init.

ops_lead: so two faults: role change caused multipart fallback and client refactor removed explicit SSE tag on fallback -> cleartext uploads.

nina.ops: mitigation plan: 1) immediate rollback of uploader to 2.3.7 (done), 2) identify all objects uploaded by 2.4.0 and mark for re-encryption, 3) lock janitor to prevent deletions, 4) notify impacted customers + legal.

infra_sam: I pushed a hold for archive janitor on the affected prefixes.

ops_lead: can we re-encrypt in-place? S3 doesn't let you change server-side-encryption without rewriting object. we need to copy the object with SSE-CMEK or SSE-S3 and then update catalog.

sec_bot: recommended script: use aws s3 cp with --metadata-directive REPLACE and --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id <kms-arn>. sample below.

ops_lead: paste the script and I'll run in a controlled worker pool.

infra_sam:
```bash
# re-encrypt detected objects
for obj in $(cat impacted_objects.txt); do
  aws s3 cp "s3://archive-bucket/$obj" "s3://archive-bucket/$obj" --metadata-directive REPLACE --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111:key/rewrap-key-1
done
```

ops_lead: good. add concurrency limiter and retry on 5xx.

nina.ops: customer notification draft: "We detected a subset of backup uploads that did not have server-side encryption applied due to a deployment/iam race. We have re-encrypted the copies and verified integrity. No signs of exfiltration. We will offer an incident report and call with infra team." Any legal concerns? @legal_claire

legal_claire: notify customers as a precaution. preserve evidence (audit logs, object versions) and do not delete originals until forensics signoff. suggest offering optional remediation assistance.

sec_bot: forensics checklist appended: collect cloudtrail events for PutObject/PutObjectCopy, IAM policy diffs, uploader deployment diffs, timestamps, and S3 version-ids.

ops_lead: actionables recap: 1) rollback (done). 2) run re-encrypt job with concurrency 20, retain original versions, tag re-encrypted objects with `x-redwood-reencrypted-by=incident/1876543211`. 3) revert IAM policy narrowing and make pre-deploy test that performs multipart-init + verifies SSE header on fallback. 4) add deployment guardrail in CI: integration test that simulates multipart failure and validates SSE enforced. 5) add alert: key SSE header absent on PutObject.

infra_sam: starting re-encrypt job now against file impacted_objects.txt (18 entries). will post progress.

ops_lead: create ticket SEC-4188 and PR for CI guardrail. link in thread.

nina.ops: PR: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-4188.working. patch will explicitly set SSE header in all client paths and add fallthrough assertion.

tom_h: after first 6 objects re-encrypted, checksums match expected from catalog. good.

sec_bot: monitoring: sse-enforcement alert rate returning to baseline.

legal_claire: confirm we retained originals and exported audit to secure bucket for 400 days.

ops_lead: originals retained (S3 versioning on). exported cloudtrail slices to legal bucket.

nina.ops: follow-ups: 1) weekly audit to surface any PutObject missing SSE headers, 2) IAM policy review for roles that perform multipart, 3) update runbook for backup uploads to include explicit SSE header enforcement.

sec_bot: Incident SEC-4188 status: mitigated -> postmortem. assigned to infra_sam.

ops_lead: thanks team. will schedule postmortem and customer comms.
